newsitem.title: UK: UK manufacturing output down 0.1% in March.
newsitem.headline: UK manufacturing output down 0.1% in March.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) released the following seasonally adjusted data on UK industrial production in March:
MINING/QUARRYING INCLUDING OIL AND GAS EXTRACTION

NOTE - Consensus forecast was for industrial production to rise by 0.4 percent in March for a year-on-year rise of 1.2 percent. Manufacturing output was expected up 0.3 percent on the month, giving a year-on-year rise of 1.9 percent.
The ONS said in the first quarter of 1997 over half the manufacturing industries achieved increases in production compared with the previous quarter.
Most notably food, drink and tobacco output rose 1.7 percent as did output of the electrical and optical equipment industries. Transport equipment output was 1.6 percent higher.
But rubber and plastic products output fell by 2.5 percent and the output of both the pulp, paper and publishing industries and the textiles, leather and clothing industries dropped by 0.8 percent.

Output of the durable goods industries rose by 0.7 percent compared with the previous quarter and by 2.4 percent over the same quarter a year ago, the ONS said. A fall of 2.5 percent in the output of cars was offset by a 4.2 percent increase in the output of other durable goods.

In the non-durable goods sector, a 1.6 percent decrease in clothing and footwear output was balanced by the 1.7 percent jump in food, drink and tobacco. Output of non-durable goods was 0.9 percent higher three months on three months and 0.7 percent up on the same quarter last year.
The ONS said output of the investment goods industries rose by 1.7 percent in the first quarter of 1997 versus the previous three months and was 3.8 percent up on a year ago.
The ONS said export production was holding up, particularly in chemicals and engineering.
